text: The hungry man is an Irish folkloric figure. His Irish names are féar gortach and far gorta. He is a variant of the hungry grass legend. The hungry grass strikes any walker with insatiable hunger. The hungry man is an insistent vision of a starving beggar. He stands by the roadside with his hand out, silently asking for alms. Giving the hungry man food brings good luck. Like the hungry grass, the figure is thought to have arisen after the famine of the 1840s. He may also tap into older folkloric traditions. The figure warns of hunger and rewards the generous.
